official_dependencies.duckdb: v1.5.5, archive and DLL hashes in the official dependency receipt, DLL hash in campaign environments

measured_findings.finding: Packed SPI is a scan-oriented physical expert, not a general faster engine.
measured_findings.evidence: In the normal 2,000-row case, packed full scan was 0.4214 ms versus 16.001 ms for legacy SPI and 0.5675 ms for SQLite. At 20,000 rows, packed full scan was 4.831 ms versus 153.649 ms for legacy SPI and 5.617 ms for SQLite. LMDB scans were faster than packed SPI in every case, including 0.2264 ms normal and 2.2001 ms scale.
measured_findings.boundary: Three-seed medians from one sequential Windows host. This does not establish statistical dominance or service-tail behavior.

measured_findings.finding: Mature embedded engines lead most load, update and durable-commit measurements.
measured_findings.evidence: Normal-case load was 83.242 ms for packed SPI, 25.619 ms for SQLite, 24.855 ms for redb, 24.589 ms for LMDB and 23.160 ms for RocksDB. Updates were 85.940 ms for packed SPI versus 39.559 ms for SQLite and 22.575 ms for RocksDB. Durable single-row commit p50 was 9,450.3 microseconds for packed SPI versus 2,628.8 for SQLite and 2,690.9 for RocksDB.
measured_findings.boundary: Durability settings and transaction semantics differ as recorded in the capability ledger. No universal score is valid.

measured_findings.finding: The current DuckDB result is a slow prepared-BLOB KV characterization, not an analytics result.
measured_findings.evidence: Normal-case DuckDB load was 3,394.035 ms, updates 1,105.511 ms and warm point p50 287.6 microseconds.
measured_findings.boundary: DuckDB used prepared BLOB primary-key statements, one thread and a 64 MiB memory floor. SPI has no typed columnar analytics API in this checkpoint.

measured_findings.finding: PostgreSQL BYTEA timings include server and transport work and are not embedded-call measurements.
measured_findings.evidence: Normal PostgreSQL medians were 195.478 ms load, 43.470 ms updates, 325.0 microseconds durable mutation p50 and 1.554 ms full scan. Large-value load was 146.245 ms and scale load was 2,050.637 ms.
measured_findings.boundary: New owned PostgreSQL 18.4 loopback cluster per case, fsync/full_page_writes/synchronous_commit on, serializable transactions, prepared SQL over TCP. Cache-cleared results are unavailable.

measured_findings.finding: Packed scan bottlenecks moved from fragmented reads toward page-miss bytes, checksum work and allocation traffic under constrained cache.
measured_findings.evidence: In the diagnostic 1 KiB case, packed warm reads processed 32.612 MB and requested 34.720 MB of Rust allocations. The normal packed full scan used 48 read calls and 193,528 bytes versus 8,000 calls and 352,000 bytes for legacy SPI, but its small-cache warm phase exposed the larger temporary page and output traffic.
measured_findings.boundary: Diagnostic allocator counts exclude native allocations. Memory samples include the harness and output buffers. Diagnostic timings are not accepted performance evidence. MB uses decimal bytes. The two counters were 32,612,384 read bytes and 34,719,792 allocation-request bytes.

measured_findings.finding: Durable publication is a material SPI cost and remains correctness-constrained.
measured_findings.evidence: One legacy normal diagnostic single-commit phase covering the 30-mutation stream attributed 74.265 ms to data sync, 149.809 ms to manifest sync and 34.217 ms to manifest replacement. Packed attribution was similar at 78.376 ms, 151.799 ms and 48.056 ms.
measured_findings.boundary: These are nested timers for a phase containing 30 commits, not per-commit costs. Do not sum them or remove sync_all, manifest publication or directory barriers.

measured_findings.finding: Small caches, large values and post-mutation scans expose remaining packed SPI losses.
measured_findings.evidence: At 1 KiB requested cache, packed point median was 24.6 microseconds versus SQLite 9.5 and redb 7.1. With 4 KiB values, packed scans were 8.7804 ms versus SQLite 4.2383 and LMDB 1.5668. Normal post-mutation scans were 0.7309 ms packed versus SQLite 0.6859 and LMDB 0.3326.
measured_findings.boundary: LMDB has OS-managed caching. RocksDB may read these small datasets from memtables despite a small block cache. These are not equal total-memory experiments.

measured_findings.finding: Resource totals include adapter lifecycle costs and cannot rank total engine efficiency.
measured_findings.evidence: Normal diagnostic RocksDB measured 4,281.25 ms phase CPU, of which 4,125 ms was in cache-cleared reads that repeatedly close and reopen the database. Normal legacy and packed SPI measured 328.125 and 140.625 ms across measured phases. Their maximum sampled working sets were 20,254,720 and 11,030,528 bytes.
measured_findings.boundary: One seed per case. These are instrumented phase totals including harness work, not CPU per operation. Native allocations and PostgreSQL server resources are unmeasured. Tiny-cache working set did not improve: legacy 10,498,048 versus packed 10,633,216 bytes.

measured_findings.finding: File lengths and maintenance costs need engine-specific interpretation.
measured_findings.evidence: Normal final file lengths were packed SPI 193,600 bytes and SQLite 200,704, but scale SQLite was smaller at 1,650,688 versus packed SPI 1,935,168. LMDB reported 1,073,750,016 bytes with a 1 GiB map configuration. PostgreSQL size covers relations, not shared cluster or WAL files.
measured_findings.boundary: Logical lengths are not allocated device bytes or RAM. LMDB sync is not compaction, DuckDB checkpoint is not vacuum, and PostgreSQL reconnect is not restart. No maintenance or size ranking establishes feature parity.

next_optimization_priorities.target: Investigate durable publication latency without weakening barriers.
next_optimization_priorities.acceptance: Separate data synchronization, manifest write, manifest sync, replacement and directory synchronization. Test batching only when snapshot visibility, crash cuts and recovery semantics remain unchanged.

next_optimization_priorities.target: Reduce packed page-miss read amplification and temporary allocations under small caches and large values.
next_optimization_priorities.acceptance: Retain materialized and direct-base controls, exact checksum coverage, full output checks, persistent-byte comparisons and the legacy fallback. Measure read calls, read bytes, requested allocations, live allocations and working set separately.

next_optimization_priorities.target: Add cost-aware physical-expert admission and routing.
next_optimization_priorities.acceptance: Use workload evidence to choose legacy or packed execution, charge construction and retirement costs, preserve exact fallback behavior and keep opt-in controls until adversarial workload shifts are measured.

next_optimization_priorities.target: Build typed shared APIs before claiming SQL, analytics, search or vector comparisons.
next_optimization_priorities.acceptance: Implement exact typed semantics and matching SPI interfaces first. Keep DuckDB analytics, PostgreSQL SQL, full-text, vector and distributed transaction domains as explicit gaps.
Add native allocation and OS-cache accounting, larger-than-RAM cases, storage-full and sync-error matrices, device-level power-loss tests and foreground maintenance bounds.

unsupported_domains: General SQL planning, typed relational schemas, joins and SQL OLTP
Typed columnar analytics and analytical joins
Distributed transactions, replication and network failure handling
Equal total-memory or OS-cache budgets across engines
final_boundary: This checkpoint demonstrates a durable native SPI substrate, several opt-in exact storage and scan experts, and a source-identified binary-KV comparison harness. It does not complete Track A, implement automatic mixture-of-experts routing, establish production readiness or prove superiority over every database.

rejected_attempt.reason: Initial PostgreSQL runner hung after startup on Windows inherited output pipes and hit the outer timeout. The server process was gone and its port free. Old files remain locally. File-backed capture fix passed regression tests and all three replacement campaigns.
